findings.text: the head-row has two consecutive tr start tags (<tr><tr><td>head ...), so the before/after basetemp table is malformed; the commit under review edited this fragment but did not repair the row the prior review flagged here.

the head arm's header names revision da95e9148 with "working tree: uncommitted prune-fix changes" while the manifest's after_suite.revision asserts the commit 586d3d890, so the gate-to-commit tie rests on the content digest alone; the log does not name the commit it measured.

neither the regression reproduction (the watcher test red twice at the unfixed head) nor the tests/test_watch_arming_isolation.py "8 passed" artifact has a named on-disk log; both are named in test_logs' absence and found only in the run's resume stream, so a reader cannot open the red arm.

the base arm runs 20 files (397 items) and the head arm runs 21 (401 items, adding tests/test_test_watchers_are_reaped.py), so the arms are not the same file list and the retention fragment's "same file list" prose no longer describes the final head arm; zero added failures is therefore over a superset head.

the autouse fixture's name says 'armed_by_this_test' but it reaps every reapable producer under the worker basetemp at each test's teardown and walks the whole tree (watcher_record_dirs rglob) per test, so its reach and cost are broader than its name and both grow with the accumulated basetemp under retention 'all'.

item_verdicts.call_sites: no production call sites added; the change is confined to tests/conftest.py and two evidence fragments
item_verdicts.diff: read against base da95e9148: one commit adding _SEAT_RECORDS_DIR, preserve_seat_records(root) (copies crew/watch/*.lock of every record under root into root/_seat-records/<rel>, skipping the mirror itself) and an autouse function-scoped fixture reap_watch_producers_armed_by_this_test(tmp_path, tmp_path_factory) that, on teardown, signals reapable_watch_pids(root) with SIGTERM, awaits exit, then mirrors the records; plus the two evidence fragments (a new 'The reap runs before the prune' section and a gate-count update). I confirmed the premise in the installed pytest: _pytest.tmpdir.tmp_path removes the per-test dir at that test's own teardown when tmp_path_retention_policy is 'failed' and the call phase passed, and the new fixture requests tmp_path so it finalizes first, giving the reap-before-prune ordering it claims.
item_verdicts.done_when: The node's gate re-ran at the unfixed head and after: base 56b32133 (20 files) 395 passed/2 skipped EXIT=0; head (21 files, +tests/test_test_watchers_are_reaped.py) 398 passed/3 skipped EXIT=0, zero added failures against the base arm's empty failure_ids. The regression reproduction is corroborated from the run's own stream: test_a_watcher_armed_by_a_child_session_is_not_left_running failed twice at the unfixed head on the armed_projects(child_base) assertion ("the child session left no seat record for 'proj'"), and passes after the fix. I re-ran tests/test_test_watchers_are_reaped.py + tests/test_watch_arming_isolation.py at the committed head 586d3d890: 10 passed, 1 skipped, EXIT=0.
item_verdicts.goal: The increment under review is the single commit the run gained since its prior review (da95e9148 -> 586d3d890): it repairs the regression the retention change itself introduced, where keeping only failed tests' temporary trees pruned a passing arming test's seat record at that test's own teardown, before the session-scoped watch reaper could read it, so a live producer could no longer be attributed and the session's liveness scan failed. The commit adds a function-scoped autouse fixture that reaps the recorded producers under the run basetemp at each test's teardown before tmp_path is pruned, mirrors the seat records into <basetemp>/_seat-records so a later reader still finds them, and leaves the session-end /proc scan unchanged; the merged-head watcher test passes and the unrecorded-producer leak still fails the session.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, commits [da95e9148, 586d3d890], baseline_suite and after_suite both completed true with failure_count 0 and failure_ids [], so added_failure_count is 0 and added_failure_ids []. The manifest's after_suite.revision names the committed head 586d3d890 while the head gate log's own header names da95e9148 with "working tree: uncommitted prune-fix changes" (content digest 35a1f2be...), so the gate-to-commit tie rests on the digest alone; my re-run at the literal commit closes that tie for the watcher files.
item_verdicts.write_paths: read; the commit touches tests/conftest.py and the two evidence fragments docs/evidence/fragments/one-typesafe-model-picker/suite-cleans-its-temp.html and .../suite-tidies-and-blocks-jev-http.html, all inside the node's declared write paths; no production module is touched. The declared figure path docs/figures/one-typesafe-model-picker/suite-tidies-and-blocks-jev-http remains unwritten (a prior-review follow-on, still open).

justifications.durability: The fixture is load-bearing — without it the merged-head watcher test fails (reproduced twice in the run's own stream) — and it signals by record with the home-identity refusal in reapable_watch_pids, so a drifted or reused pid cannot aim a teardown signal at another run's watcher. The cut is cost and breadth: it rglobs the whole basetemp (watcher_record_dirs) at every test's teardown, so under retention 'all' the per-test walk grows with the accumulated tree, and it reaps every reapable producer under the worker's root, not only the current test's; the _seat-records mirror also accumulates within a session.
justifications.evidence: Both arms are green with EXIT=0 and zero failures, my independent re-run at the literal committed head is green (10 passed/1 skipped), and the regression reproduction is corroborated from the run's own stream (two red arms on the armed_projects assertion). The cuts are real: (a) the head gate log's header names da95e9148 with uncommitted prune-fix changes rather than the committed 586d3d890, so the log alone cannot tie the gate to the commit (a recurrence of the prior review's finding); (b) the reproduction and the 'tests/test_watch_arming_isolation.py 8 passed' artifact have no named on-disk log — both live only in the resume stream; (c) the two arms are not the same file list (base 20 files, head 21), so the 'zero added failures' is over a superset head and the retention fragment's 'same file list' prose no longer describes the final head arm.
justifications.fit: Names follow mechanism, the subject is conventional with a body and no AI-attribution trailer, and the fragments document the increment. Two cuts: the fixture is named reap_watch_producers_armed_by_this_test while it reaps every recorded producer under the basetemp; and the commit edited suite-cleans-its-temp.html but left in place the malformed <tr><tr> row the prior review flagged on that file, so a defect in a file it touched survives.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The commit repairs exactly the regression the goal names: the retention change pruned a passing arming test's seat record before the session reaper read it, and the fix reaps at the arming test's own teardown, before tmp_path is removed, then preserves the records for a later reader. The premise is verified in the installed pytest source (_pytest.tmpdir.tmp_path) and the merged-head watcher test passes at the committed revision; the cut is that the fix is a bounded mitigation — it reaches only producers that wrote a record and reaps every producer under the basetemp rather than just the current test's, so the session-end scan remains the backstop for an unrecorded producer and the fixture's name overstates its reach.
justifications.scope_discipline: Every changed path is inside the declared write paths and the change stays within the suite: tests/conftest.py and the two evidence fragments, no production module, no field or file the goal does not imply. The only open scope item is the previously declared figure path, which the commit did not add to (it predates this increment).
